Major U.S. stock indices rose to all-time closing highs Monday, but the Dow industrials ended just shy of a new record as technology shares suffered a late sell-off.
Bonds fell on news of an unexpected jump in August U.S. home sales.
The dollar rose to a 32-month high against the Japanese yen after comments by Japanese finance officials sent Japanese investors scurrying to find higher interest rates overseas.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 9.25 points to 5,882.17. The blue chip index earlier hit a session peak of 5,907.32, topping Sept. 23's record high finish of 5,894.74.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,295 to 1,069 on heavy volume of 388 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks set a record, up 1.14 to 687.33, surpassing Sept. 20's closing high of 687.02.
The NYSE Composite index added 1.06 to 367.33, eclipsing Friday's record peak of 366.27. The average price per share rose 11 cents.
The Nasdaq Composite index lost 3.13 to 1,226.92 after earlier rising nearly four points.

The bond market erased an early advance and turned lower after the Commerce Department said August single-family homes sales jumped 4.7 percent to an annual rate of 832,000 units -- the highest rate in more than a decade.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 7/32, raising the yield to 6.92 percent from 6.91 percent at Friday's close.
While home sales pressured bonds, analysts said equity investors were relieved to see signs of economic strength that will aid corporate profits.

In Tokyo, the dollar powered above 111.20 yen, the previous 1996 high set in July. It reached 111.68 yen -- its highest level since hitting 111.75 in January 1994 -- before settling back to 111.37 yen in New York, up from 110.90 late Friday.
The dollar also rose to 1.5291 German marks early Monday -- its highest since July 8 -- before slipping to 1.5250 marks in late trading vs. 1.5244 late Friday.

The strong dollar and stock rally diluted interest in precious metals on the New York Mercantile Exchange's COMEX division. December gold fell $2.30 to $380.50 an ounce after falling to $380.10 during the session, a new three-year low for the December contract.
Grain prices tumbled as weather improved in the Midwest.
Soybeans for November delivery fell 25-1/4 cents to $7.58 a bushel and December corn ended 6-1/2 cents lower at $2.96-3/4, the lowest closing price since Jan. 29, both at the Chicago Board of Trade.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange oil prices ended lower after last week's rally. Talk that a deal to allow Iraq to sell oil may be revived fuelled selling.

November crude oil fell 22 cents to $24.38 a barrel and October unleaded gasoline fell 1.89 cents to 62.71 cents a gallon. October heating oil edged up 0.02 cent to 71.51 cents a gallon. October contracts expired on Monday.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 share index reversed modest early losses to end the day at 3,953.7 points, up 7.3 points. In Tokyo, the key 225-share Nikkei average finished up 9.38 points at 21,556.40.
